content.text: The text combines Laurence Hope’s *India’s Love Lyrics*, portraying sensual, tragic, fatalistic love amid Indian landscapes, with the novel *Oh, Money!* and military memoirs. In *Oh, Money!*, millionaire Stanley G. Fulton disguises himself as genealogist John Smith, boards with Maggie Duff, and observes relatives whose sudden wealth produces vanity, addiction, anxiety, or—eventually—self-knowledge. Smith visits James Blaisdell’s book-lined room at the end of the hall, helps Mellicent and Donald Gray unite, and later travels from Hillerton to South America before returning as Fulton. He and Maggie reconcile, marry, and plan philanthropic projects. The memoir recounts the Ninety-Third Highlanders’ march from Oude through Shahjehanpore, Bareilly, Moradabad, Saharunpore, Umballa, and Kalka to Subathoo. An appendix recounts the alleged revenge killing of Major Neill at Augur in 1887, linked to executions during the 1857 uprising.
